facts.heading: Anxiety started in September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time and it got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Work situation changed
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years. Her deputy head left, and she was asked to step up.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah keeps thinking someone will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Nighttime rehearsal of thoughts
facts.content: Hannah rehearses what to say and what others will think on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Fear of being out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Fear of being incompetent
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is incapable of the job.
facts.evidence: That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Email rewriting anxiety
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of being stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Governor's treatment
facts.content: Mr. Hargraves has been kind to Hannah.
facts.evidence: He has been nothing but kind.

facts.heading: Feeling of deception
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: I feel like I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Feeling of pretense
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feeling like a child
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother's career
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Mother's reputation
facts.content: Hannah's mother was brilliant and people still praise her.
facts.evidence: She was brilliant. Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Comparison to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares everything she does to what her mother might have done better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do I think would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's advice
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Mother's advice effect
facts.content: Hearing her mother's advice makes Hannah feel like she is making a fuss.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning. She falls asleep fine.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine.

facts.heading: Drinking coffee to cope
facts.content: Hannah drinks a lot of coffee to get through the day. This started about the second week of term.
facts.evidence: since about the second week of term i drink a lot of coffee to get through today which i know

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Exhaustion from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day due to pretending.
facts.evidence: I am exhausted by the end of every day. Just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice on feelings
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben suggested she should enjoy her situation.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feelings when partner speaks
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben gives that advice.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner's view on fixing problems
facts.content: Ben believes that if something is a problem, Hannah should fix it.
facts.evidence: He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it.

facts.heading: Loss of school friends
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school. She is now their line manager.
facts.evidence: Not anymore, not really. Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Missing school environment
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and the daily experience of children getting something new.
facts.evidence: The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Missing past school days
facts.content: Hannah misses her class and the time spent in the corridor with friends.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Desire for deeper motion
facts.content: Hannah expressed a desire for deeper motion.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her.

facts.heading: Tears about fear and future
facts.content: Hannah cried after saying yes to something and the tears were about fear and never going back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays while walking in the lakes.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays, we went walking in the lakes

facts.heading: Distraction from school thoughts
facts.content: During the lake trip, Hannah did not think about school for ten days.
facts.evidence: And I didn't think about school once for ten days

facts.heading: Pre-term distress
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck and could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This lasted for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A trail of laughing. A good email. It held for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Goal to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do her job without feeling like a fraud. This involves not rehearsing in meetings and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal to relax in evening
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without stomach knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feelings after stating goals
facts.content: Hannah felt light and lighter when stating her goals out loud. She also felt a bit tearful.
facts.evidence: A lightful. Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: Sharing bad news with Ben
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad things are. Ben does not know how bad things are.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about before I am.

facts.heading: Fear of telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah finds telling Ben scary. She worries he would be hurt that she did not say sooner.
facts.evidence: Scary. He would probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Plan to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben this week. She considers it a reason not to keep it to herself.
facts.evidence: I might try this week. Would it be a reason to keep it to yourself?

facts.heading: Helpful time to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah thinks a quiet moment on Saturday morning over breakfast would help her tell Ben.
facts.evidence: if I choose a quiet moment not on a Sunday evening then I'm Saturday morning perhaps he is always in a good mood then

facts.heading: Try evening notebook again
facts.content: Hannah is considering trying the evening notebook again for one week. She plans to write one line by the kettle to avoid forgetting.
facts.evidence: would you try the evening notebook again just for a week even one line I could I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget
